scheme: B1: close grain, so it can be shaped and smoothed well
B1: hard and durable, so it survives rough use
B1: a non-toxic finish, e.g. food-safe oil or water-based varnish

long.q: A school workshop must make 30 identical pine boxes. (a) Explain two benefits of using a jig or template for marking out and drilling the parts. (b) Name a suitable corner joint for the boxes and give one reason for your choice.
scheme: B1: (a) every part is identical and accurate, so quality is consistent
B1: (a) faster: no need to measure and mark out each piece
B1: (b) a suitable joint, e.g. comb (finger), lap (rebate) or dowel joint
B1: (b) a matching reason, e.g. a comb joint's large gluing area makes it strong; dowel holes are quick to drill with a jig

questions.q: What is the main purpose of product analysis?
o: To find out how and why an existing product was designed and made
questions.why: Consider function, materials, manufacture, user and sustainability.

long.q: Explain how a designer could make an electric kettle more sustainable. Give two design changes and say how each one helps.
scheme: B1: a change, e.g. recycled or recyclable plastic marked with its recycling code
B1: explained, e.g. less new material used; easy to sort at end of life
B1: a second change, e.g. screws not glue so it can be taken apart; a replaceable element; better insulation
B1: explained, e.g. parts can be repaired or separated for recycling; less energy used to reboil

long.q: Explain why a manufacturer would want a dimensioned orthographic drawing of a product rather than a 3D sketch.

questions.q: A potential divider with an LDR can be used to
o: switch on a light when it gets dark
questions.why: The LDR's resistance rises in the dark.
The follower rises and falls.

questions.q: In a circuit, what does an LDR do?
o: It switches at a set temperature
Its resistance changes with light level
questions.why: Used as a light sensor in a potential divider.

long.q: A potential divider has a 9 V supply, R1 = 10 kΩ at the top and R2 = 5 kΩ at the bottom. (a) Calculate the output voltage across R2, showing your working. (b) R2 is replaced by an LDR. Explain what happens to the output voltage as it gets darker.
scheme: M1: Vout = Vin × R2 ÷ (R1 + R2)
A1: 3 V (with the unit)
B1: (b) the LDR's resistance increases as light falls
B1: (b) so it takes a bigger share of the supply and Vout rises
long.ans: (a) 3 V; (b) Vout rises as it gets darker
